answers.answer: Honest defense with the confidence stated up front: the anchor is [FACT] Vardhman FY20 raw-material = 54% of revenue, and my derived yarn share (~50-60% of the stack) and ~$1-2.50 fibre/value-core garment are [ESTIMATE, MED] (KB1 YARN_LEVEL_ANCHOR / TWO_NUMBER_FRAME). I do NOT claim 54% is the cluster's yarn share; my KB1 explicitly lists the failure mode 'quoting 54% as the cluster's yarn share rather than a single-firm MED-confidence anchor.' The anchor could be off by a factor at these steps: (1) Vardhman is vertically-integrated group revenue, not a Ludhiana job-work conversion, so its raw-material/revenue ratio includes captive spinning economics and a product mix that is not our 300-500g bought-dyed capsule; (2) FY20 is a single stale year and a single firm; (3) raw-material-to-REVENUE is not the same denominator as raw-material-to-ex-factory-CONVERSION-cost (revenue carries a brand/retail margin we do not, which mechanically DEFLATES the raw-material share vs a thin CMT stack). That third point actually cuts toward yarn being a LARGER share of a pure-conversion stack than 54%, i.e. it does not threaten 'yarn sets the level.' On the stress test: my core takeaway is 'yarn anchors the LEVEL and is NOT the constraint; the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate is the uncertainty' (conflicts_and_dominance[1]). If the true yarn share were 70%, 'yarn is not the constraint' survives comfortably (yarn is even more dominant and even better anchored, so effort still belongs on the rate). If the true share were 40%, the knit+LINK conversion portion is proportionally LARGER, which strengthens, not weakens, 'chase the [UNKNOWN] rate not cheaper yarn.' So the takeaway is robust to the anchor being off in either direction; what the anchor buys is the LEVEL's rough magnitude (~$1-2.50 fibre), and that is why I hold it [ESTIMATE, MED], not [FACT]. GAP: the spec does not carry an explicit sensitivity table for the 40%/70% cases; I reason it here from the frame's structure, so support is partial on the exact numeric bracket.
answers.grounded_in: capabilities[0].method + capabilities[1].method (two-number frame); glossary 'two-number frame'; KB1 YARN_LEVEL_ANCHOR (54% Vardhman [FACT], ~$1-2.50 [ESTIMATE, MED], 'single-firm MED-confidence anchor' failure mode, order-of-magnitude premium caveat); conflicts_and_dominance[1]; validation_checklist item 2.
answers.gap_note: The spec correctly labels 54% as [FACT] and the derived share/level as [ESTIMATE, MED] and even pre-lists the over-hardening failure mode, so the honesty is intact. What is MISSING is an explicit written sensitivity showing the 'yarn is not the constraint' conclusion survives at 40% and 70% true share (I supply that reasoning here from the frame's structure). A 'propose' item: add a one-line robustness note to the anchor so the single-anchor risk is visibly bounded rather than only implicitly handled.

answers.answer: No contradiction, and the ~25-45% is NOT a fabricated point smuggled as structure - but the honest answer is that the band's LOWER bound does rest on an implied minimum, which I must own openly. How a bounded band survives an [UNKNOWN] largest line: the LEVEL is anchored (yarn ~50-60%, ~$1-2.50 [ESTIMATE, MED]) and the OTHER conversion lines (finishing, trims/labels/pack, QC, EPF/ESI on labour-bearing portion, overhead/margin) are separately bounded; only the knit+LINK lines are [UNKNOWN]. I bound those two lines NOT by a Ludhiana quote but by the FF-costing cross-check used SHAPE-ONLY and [DOWNGRADED] to LOW-MED (KB1 FF_COSTING_CROSSCHECK). That cross-check supplies a plausibility RANGE for the per-piece knit+link contribution, which is what lets the total be a band rather than an open interval. The '~25-45% of conversion' is my [ESTIMATE] of the knit+LINK SHARE of the conversion subtotal, derived from that shape range against the anchored other lines - it is a labelled estimate of a proportion, not a covert Rs/piece rate; you cannot back out a single fabricated rate from a 20-point-wide share band. Honest concession the adversary is right to press: the band's LOWER bound (A2 ~$3.5) does encode an implied MINIMUM plausible knit+LINK contribution (near the low end of the shape cross-check); if a real quote came back BELOW that implied minimum, the floor would drop. That is exactly why the whole band is [ESTIMATE, LOW-MED] and why conflicts_and_dominance[2] says 'a fabricated point on the [UNKNOWN] knit+LINK rate would corrupt the whole model, so bands stand and the missing rate stays [UNKNOWN].' The band is honest precisely BECAUSE it is wide and low-confidence; it does not pretend to the precision a quote would give. 'One quote run halves every band' means collapsing that shape-derived width to a real rate, which is coherent with holding the rate [UNKNOWN] now.

answers.answer: Legitimate distinction: the FF-costing study licenses the SHAPE (the link=~60%-of-knitting RATIO and the linker-as-daily-ceiling logic) but not the LEVEL, and I must be honest that even the ratio is only [DOWNGRADED] LOW-MED, not scale-free. What the study gives: knitting ~$0.74/pc, linking ~$0.45/pc (~60% of knitting), a finishing chain figure, and per-operator-day throughput shape (KB1 FF_COSTING_CROSSCHECK). I use it SHAPE-ONLY for two things: (a) the RELATIVE proportion link:knit ~60:100, and (b) the ceiling logic that linking is the labour-heavy, throughput-limiting seam step (so linking is subcontracted LAST). Why the ratio transfers better than the level: the level (absolute $/pc) is a foreign-productivity-and-wage artifact and Ludhiana labour is cheaper, so the ABSOLUTE numbers do not transfer and I never quote them as Ludhiana. The RATIO is more transferable because it reflects the relative labour content of linking vs knitting (linking is inherently more hand-labour-intensive per piece), a physical-process property that is more stable across wage levels than the absolute cost. HONEST CONCESSION the adversary correctly forces: the 60% ratio is NOT perfectly scale-free - it is still a productivity-and-wage artifact, because if Ludhiana's knitting-vs-linking productivity gap differs from the study's, the ratio shifts. My KB does not claim the ratio is scale-invariant; it labels the whole cross-check [DOWNGRADED] LOW-MED precisely so it 'bounds a band and never collapses to a Ludhiana quote.' So: the linker-is-the-bottleneck claim and linking-last verdict inherit LOW-MED confidence, and if a real Ludhiana quote run returned link < ~40% of knit, both would weaken. That is a stated limitation, not a hidden over-claim. GAP: my spec asserts the ratio is 'transferable' as shape without an explicit caveat that the ratio ITSELF is not fully scale-free; I supply that caveat here, so support is partial on the transferability claim's rigor.

answers.answer: 'B2 most likely' is a real evidence-weighted lean on QUALITATIVE structure, not a claim that the [UNKNOWN] FOB number already favors B2 - and it is not the same 'never chose an implementation' error, because I DO name what would flip it. The lean is grounded NOT in the missing FOB price but in the counter-analysis: B2 (single-vertical full-package FOB) structurally DELETES two of the four honest counters to 'buy' - QC fragmentation and coordination load - by collapsing QC inside one accountable vendor with a captive-spinning margin that can partly subsidise the buyer (KB2 B2_FULLPACKAGE_FOB; conflicts_and_dominance[3]). B1 (multi-job-worker mesh) carries those two fragilities and the 'no captive cushion' one. So on the QUALITATIVE counter-map, B2 answers more fragilities - that is the basis of 'most likely,' and it is qualitative, not a fabricated FOB number. What B2 LOSES on and what would make B1 win: B2 has higher MOQ (~300-1,000+ vs B1 ~100-300) and loses material/colour control. So B1 wins if the observed FOB MOQ is too high to fund at capsule scale (blows the first cheque / dye-lot plan) OR if material control / a controlled hero colour (B3-like) is worth more than the coordination saving. Why 'B2 most likely' is not equally 'B1 most likely': B2 removes MORE of the enumerated fragilities for a first-time thin operator with limited coordination capacity, which is the launch reality; that asymmetry is the evidence. It is a LEAN, explicitly held pending the [UNKNOWN] FOB price+MOQ quote run (escalation_triggers[1]), and I would NOT state it as decided. Honest limit: 'most likely' is a soft directional word; the deciding number is [UNKNOWN], so I present it as 'the most likely flip, decidable now by one quote run,' never as a settled verdict - which is materially different from the original consensus that never distinguished the implementations at all.

answers.gap_note: The lean is qualitatively grounded (B2 deletes 2 of 4 counters) and the flip-to-B1 condition (FOB MOQ too high to fund / material-control value) is nameable, so this is not an un-tested assertion. No material gap; the only softness is the word 'most likely' itself, which the spec already couples to 'decidable now by the [UNKNOWN] quote run,' keeping it a lean not a verdict.

answers.answer: I can reproduce the STRUCTURE and the DIRECTION of the >1.0 result without fabricating the rate, but I must be honest that 'above 1.0' is a labelled directional [ESTIMATE] driven by the utilisation-starvation of a single-program capsule, NOT a fully-computed arithmetic point - and that is exactly how my spec frames it. The formula (KB2 OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN): breakeven_utilisation = owned_fixed_period_cost / ((jobwork_unit_rate - owned_variable_unit_cost) * period_capacity). The honest illustration for the sub-$20k used Cixing-class, one A2 program: the DENOMINATOR is the per-piece saving (jobwork_rate minus owned_variable) times the machine's period capacity. Two things drive breakeven above 1.0 at launch WITHOUT needing the exact rate: (1) a capsule running ONE A2 program hard still uses only a fraction of a dedicated machine-year's capacity, so realised utilisation is low; (2) the per-piece SAVING (jobwork_rate - owned_variable) is small in absolute terms at capsule volumes relative to the owned fixed period cost (machine amortisation + a programmer/operator seat + power + space), so the numerator/denominator ratio exceeds achievable utilisation. The point I am honest about: I cannot state a NUMERIC breakeven (e.g. '1.4') without the [UNKNOWN] jobwork_rate, because that rate sits in the denominator. So 'above 1.0 at launch' is an [ESTIMATE, MED] that subcontract wins BECAUSE owned utilisation is starved (conflicts_and_dominance[4]: 'at capsule scale owned utilisation is starved so subcontracting wins on unit cost'), and the crossover cannot be LOCATED (given a number) until the rate is quoted. It is neither a hidden fabricated rate nor pure formula theatre: it is a direction argued from the starvation of utilisation, with the exact breakeven held [UNKNOWN]-pending-rate. GAP: my spec says the illustration 'comes out above 1.0' with 'placeholder inputs'; it does NOT publish those placeholder numbers, so I cannot show a fully numeric worked case here - the support is partial on the arithmetic, full on the direction and the reason.

answers.answer: The boundary is a HARD one and I can draw it: the iteration loop is a SAMPLING/PROTOTYPING cell whose output is protos and proven designs, NOT sellable bulk. The moment its knitted units are counted toward filling a sellable drop, it has become 'owning bulk knitting' and the utilisation/breakeven discipline (Q6) reattaches. Concretely: 'own the iteration loop' = a small used hand-flat / used linker / used press + a contracted programmer seat, justified on a SPEED/CONTROL axis because the brand's AI-design edge is bottlenecked by someone else's 2-5 week sample queue (KB2 'own the iteration loop'; conflicts_and_dominance[5]). Its purpose is overnight prototype iteration, then send ONLY proven designs to the mesh/FOB for bulk. The bright line: as soon as that cell's units are SOLD as part of a drop's fulfilled quantity, it is bulk by the back door, the SPEED justification no longer covers it, and it must pass the own-knitting breakeven (which at capsule volume comes out above 1.0 -> subcontract). Reconciliation with the machines specialist: line-capacity sizing off the linker + programmer bottleneck and any real bulk-capacity decision are the machines specialist's lane (dominance_rules machines-owns-capacity); my carve-out is a COST/CONTROL posture about a sampling cell on a speed axis, and boundaries[4] binds me to 'never present a sampling cell as owning bulk knitting.' So it is a genuine speed-axis carve-out with a policed edge (proto=allowed, sellable-bulk=forbidden-until-proven-volume), NOT an unmeasured loophole - the utilisation argument is explicitly reattached the instant output becomes sellable inventory. HONEST residual risk: the spec states the rule and the axis but does not give a numeric trip-wire (e.g. 'above N sellable units/drop from the cell = bulk'); the boundary is qualitative. That is the one place creep could hide, so I flag it as a monitoring point, not a fabricated threshold.
answers.grounded_in: conflicts_and_dominance[5] ('a small owned sampling cell + a programmer seat is defensible at launch on speed/control... this is NOT owning bulk knitting, the utilisation argument does not apply to it, and bulk still stays bought'); glossary 'own the iteration loop'; KB2 AI_ITERATION_LOOP node; boundaries[4] ('never present a sampling cell as owning bulk knitting'); dominance_rules (knit_machine_strategist owns line capacity/linker bottleneck).
answers.gap_note: The carve-out is real and the forbidden case (sampling cell presented as bulk) is explicitly banned by boundaries[4], and the machines-lane deference is honoured. The only soft edge is qualitative: there is no numeric trip-wire distinguishing 'proto iteration' from 'bulk by the back door' (e.g. a sellable-units-per-drop ceiling). 'Watch' item: consider a stated rule-of-thumb that ANY unit sold from the cell reclassifies it as bulk and reattaches the breakeven, to remove ambiguity - the principle is already there, only the sharp line is implicit.

answers.answer: The arithmetic holds and I must give the honest consequence: at real launch MOQ the true micro cost CAN sit at or above the top of the published band, and that is a stated feature (the 1.3-2x uplift), not a contradiction - but it does mean the bare band must always travel WITH the uplift caveat, never alone. Worked shape for a 3-style x 3-colour capsule (all [ESTIMATE], KB3 DYELOT_MOQ / MICRO_VOLUME_FIXED_COST): dye-lot MOQ ~150-500 kg per COLOUR is the binding floor; at ~300-400 g/sweater, 200 kg/colour ~ 500-650 sweaters of ONE colour. With 3 colours that is ~1,500-2,000 pieces of dyed-yarn commitment spread across only 3 styles -> the launch is COLOUR-starved (2-4 colours), not style-starved. Garment/CMT MOQ (~100-300 pcs/style-colour) sits BENEATH this: 3 styles x 3 colours x ~150 pcs is well inside what one colour's 500-650-sweater dye lot supports, so the dye lot, not the garment MOQ, is what forces the big cash commitment - dye-lot MOQ binds ABOVE garment MOQ. Per-style setup (sampling, programming, first-lot) amortised over these tiny per-style quantities is what lifts true micro cost to ~1.3-2x the band midpoint. Plain answer on 4 colours x 200 kg: yes, the 1.3-2x uplift can push realised A2 cost toward or above $8 (the band's top or beyond). Is the band 'simply wrong'? No - but only if it is used correctly: the A2 ~$3.5-8 band is the STEADY/repeat-volume illustration (after the dye economic-MOQ surcharge clears and setup amortises); the true MICRO launch cost is explicitly the band midpoint x1.3-2 (conflicts_and_dominance[7], validation_checklist item 8). The failure would be handing T9 the bare band for a micro launch. So the honest handling: the band is the volume-curve target, and for the actual first launch I hand T9 the volume-tier-ADJUSTED number (band x uplift), not the bare band. GAP: the published bands in the spec are stated as the headline illustrations and the 1.3-2x uplift is a separate note; a reader could take the bare band. Support is partial on presentation - the numbers are consistent but the band-vs-micro relationship must be stated every time to avoid the exact misread the adversary describes.
answers.grounded_in: capabilities[4].method (dye-lot MOQ ~150-500 kg/colour => ~500-650 sweaters/colour; garment/CMT MOQ ~100-300 pcs beneath it; true micro cost ~1.3-2x band midpoint); glossary 'dye-lot MOQ' and 'per-article ex-factory bands'; conflicts_and_dominance[6] and [7]; validation_checklist item 8; scale_and_handoff phase (volume-tier adjustment at real launch MOQ before hand-off to T9).
answers.gap_note: The arithmetic is internally consistent (dye-lot MOQ binds above garment MOQ; micro cost = band x1.3-2), so it is not wrong. The real exposure the adversary lands: the deliverable to T9 is the BAND, and at true launch MOQ the realised A2 cost can exceed the band's top - so handing the bare band risks understating cost downstream. This is handled by the 'volume-tier-adjusted input' rule but is easy to drop. 'Apply/propose': every band hand-off should be tagged with the mandatory micro-volume uplift so the band is never consumed bare for a launch-scale run.

answers.answer: I answer without naming a party, inventing a magnitude, or contradicting myself: no, the owner cannot simply ignore them, but they enter the cash plan in DIFFERENT places, and 'near-zero per garment' is a statement about the UNIT COST stack, not a magnitude claim about the total cash exposure. Two distinct mechanisms (both [UNKNOWN] amounts, both mechanism-not-accusation, N3): (1) off-paper friction / 'speed-money' - a structural, episodic discretionary-gate cost described purely as mechanism; because it is episodic and lumpy rather than per-piece, when spread over a capsule's pieces it amortises toward near-zero PER GARMENT, so it does NOT belong as a clean per-garment COGS line (boundaries[5]; glossary 'off-paper friction'). (2) inverted-duty / GST drag - acrylic (MMF) inputs taxed higher than the output, trapping working capital in slow refunds; a [FACT] mechanism biting A2, magnitude [UNKNOWN], expressed as a T9 cash-CYCLE cost, not a per-garment add (glossary 'inverted-duty / GST drag'). Resolving the apparent tension the adversary raises: 'near-zero per garment' and 'can trap cash for months' are consistent because they describe different axes - per-UNIT-cost (where both are ~zero and excluded) vs CASH-CYCLE / working-capital exposure (where the inverted-duty refund lag is real and lumpy). Is 'near-zero per garment' an illicit implicit magnitude? It is a statement that a lumpy episodic cost divided by capsule volume is small on a per-unit basis - a structural amortisation claim, not a total-amount claim; the TOTAL amount stays [UNKNOWN]. How the owner SIZES a cushion for [UNKNOWN] costs: not by a fabricated line, but by holding a CASH BUFFER against the working-capital cycle (the inverted-duty refund lag lengthens the cash-conversion cycle that G3 working-capital funding must cover), and by treating friction as an episodic contingency in the cash plan, NOT in unit cost. So the honest instruction: exclude both from the per-garment band; carry inverted-duty as a lengthened cash cycle in the T9/working-capital sizing; carry friction as an episodic contingency - amounts [UNKNOWN], never invented, never a named party. HONEST GAP: my spec says 'size a cushion' in spirit (working-capital trap, G3-adjacent) but does not give the owner a METHOD to quantify an [UNKNOWN]-magnitude buffer; the honest answer is that it stays [UNKNOWN] and is handled as buffer+contingency, which is a real limit, not a completeness claim.

answers.answer: I disentangle them cleanly and keep the US duty out of my band. Acrylic has TWO distinct penalties that owners conflate: (1) the US IMPORT duty on the finished sweater at the border - acrylic/MMF heading 6110.30.30 ~32% [FACT] - which is the ~2x outlier vs cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% [FACT] and wool 6110.11 ~16% [FACT]. This is a LANDED cost, owned by T9/unit_economics (dominance_rules landed-cost->unit_economics), and I EXCLUDE it from my ex-factory band (boundaries[2]); it never enters my factory-gate conversion number. (2) the Indian GST INVERTED-duty drag - acrylic (MMF) INPUTS taxed higher than the OUTPUT, trapping working capital in slow refunds inside India, BEFORE the goods ever ship. This is a cost/cash-CYCLE mechanism ([FACT] mechanism, magnitude [UNKNOWN]) that I own as a flag (glossary 'inverted-duty / GST drag'), expressed as a T9 cash-cycle cost, never a per-garment COGS add. So to the owner's question 'is acrylic's cost problem the ~32% US duty or the GST inversion?' - it is BOTH, but they are different animals: the ~32% is a border tax on the finished good (T9's, hits landed cost/margin) and the GST inversion is a domestic refund-lag on inputs (a working-capital drag inside the factory-gate side that I flag but do not quantify). Confirming the duty figure: cotton is ~16.5%, NOT the discredited ~7% (N5) - I state the corrected [FACT] trio and never the ~7%. What is MINE vs T9's: the GST inverted-duty MECHANISM/flag is mine to surface (it bites A2's cash cycle); the ~32% US import duty is T9's to own and I merely note it as the downstream multiplier that erases acrylic's factory-gate lead at the border - I do NOT let it leak into my conversion band.
